newsitem.title: UK: U. Utils says Manila interest may see float.
newsitem.headline: U. Utils says Manila interest may see float.

text.p: A partial float of a consortium which has won a 25-year contract to operate and develop Manila's water system, and includes Britain's United Utilities Plc, may happen within five years, Gordon Waters, managing director of the group's international division, told a press conference.
Waters said the company, which is in the consortium with Ayala and Bechtel Corp of the U.S., expected to float up to 50 percent of the consortium "no later than year five."

The consortium won the concession for the east zone of the Philippines capital in January and was expected to take over management in May, but the Manila Water Company said last month that awards would be postponed until July at the earliest.
A flotation would have to comply with government restrictions but is not unusual, industry sources said, as it can unlock value for employees who may be shareholders.
United Utilities said revenues from the project were likely to be 19 percent ahead of estimates and that it should break even in the first year of operations.
"In floating it, we will take back more than the equity we put in," United's chief executive Brian Staples said.

The consortium won the bid with an offer of 2.32 pesos per litre, around half that of other bids. Ayala said the key would be to reduce the proportion of non-revenue water, caused by leaks or pilfering, which is estimated at around 58 percent. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
